research.title: Survey on AI Conformity: Integrating Fairness, Explainability, and Performance in Ethical AI Design
research.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in society, the ethical implications of its deployment grow ever more significant. This survey explores the convergence of fairness, explainability, and performance in the design of ethical AI systems, framing them under the concept of AI conformity. I review ten pivotal studies spanning conceptual frameworks, empirical research, public perception analysis, benchmarking tools, and policy frameworks. The synthesis identifies recurring trade-offs among the three dimensions and emphasizes the importance of context-sensitive, interdisciplinary solutions. Furthermore, i highlight challenges in operationalizing ethical principles and propose future directions involving participatory design, global inclusivity, and longitudinal evaluation. The goal is to map the current landscape and chart a path toward responsible, accountable, and high-performing AI systems.

research.title: RUST TAKEAWAYS for a BETTER FUTURE
research.abstract: This paper delves into the realm of resource management and remote objects within the Rust programming language, analyzing two key publications: "RPC Resource Management and Remote Objects with Rust" by Tim and "Rust High Performance Applications" as a supporting text. We begin by establishing the problem space and background for resource management and remote objects in distributed systems, laying the groundwork for a critical examination of both papers. Subsequently, we dissect Tim's paper, dissecting its strengths and weaknesses. We delve into its proposed RPC framework and resource management solution, highlighting its contributions and limitations. Building upon this foundation, we then turn to "Rust High Performance Applications," exploring how it addresses some of the limitations identified in Tim's work. Through a comparative analysis, we assess the efficacy of both approaches, drawing upon relevant empirical data and benchmarking results. Finally, we conclude by synthesizing our findings and proposing promising directions for future research in Rust-based distributed systems.

research.title: Enhancing Telecommunications with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning: Applications and Implications
research.abstract: This systematic review explores the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in transforming telecommunications, focusing on key areas such as network optimization, fraud detection, and customer service management. As telecommunications networks become more complex, the integration of AI/ML presents solutions to tackle challenges like network congestion, service personalization, and security threats. The review highlights various global applications and innovations, particularly in network management and customer experience, with an eye on their potential relevance for Ethiopia's evolving telecommunications sector. While the Ethiopian context is not deeply analyzed, the review touches upon how local companies like Ethio Telecom and Tele Birr could benefit from global AI/ML advancements, considering Ethiopia’s unique telecommunications landscape. Through an examination of studies published between 2020 and 2024, the paper presents a comparative analysis of AI/ML strategies and their implications for improving efficiency, customer satisfaction, and security in the telecommunications industry worldwide, with specific reference to their application in Ethiopia.

research.title: Motion-Based Object Detection and Tracking: Challenges and Solutions
research.abstract: Motion-based object detection and tracking have become critical components in modern computer vision applications, ranging from autonomous vehicles to surveillance systems. With the advent of deep learning and multi-modal data fusion, numerous techniques have emerged to enhance accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. This state-of-the-art review examines recent developments in motion-based tracking, focusing on techniques, architectures, and their applications. We discuss ten influential papers that contribute to this domain, identify prevailing challenges, and propose promising directions for future research.
